tasks.title: Public data of an object
tasks.statement: Write public_data(obj): a sorted list of the names of the object's attributes (including class attributes) that do not start with an underscore and are not callable.
tasks.hint: for name in dir(obj): if not name.startswith("_") and not callable(getattr(obj, name)).

tasks.title: Command dispatcher by name
tasks.statement: Write dispatch(obj, command, *args): it calls the method of obj named cmd_<command> and returns the result. If there is no such method, raise ValueError("unknown command: <command>"). Only methods with the cmd_ prefix are accessible.
tasks.hint: handler = getattr(obj, "cmd_" + command, None); if it is None, raise ValueError.

tasks.title: Describing a function's parameters
tasks.statement: Write param_info(func): a list of tuples (name, kind, has_default) for each parameter of the function, based on its signature. The kind is the name of the inspect.Parameter.kind member (for example, KEYWORD_ONLY).
tasks.hint: for p in inspect.signature(func).parameters.values(): p.name, p.kind.name, p.default is not inspect.Parameter.empty.

tasks.title: Which values the parameters got
tasks.statement: Write resolve_args(func, *args, **kwargs): bind the call to the function's signature (bind), apply the default values, and return a plain dictionary "parameter → value". An invalid call must raise TypeError.

tasks.title: What the nested function carried off
tasks.statement: Write captured(func): a dictionary "free variable name → its value" for a closure (use __code__.co_freevars and __closure__). For a function without a closure, the result is an empty dictionary.
tasks.hint: dict(zip(func.__code__.co_freevars, (c.cell_contents for c in func.__closure__ or ()))).

tasks.title: All descendants of a class
tasks.statement: Write all_subclasses(cls): a sorted list of the names of all direct and indirect descendants of the class (without duplicates, even with diamond inheritance).
tasks.hint: Walk cls.__subclasses__() recursively and collect the names in a set.

tasks.title: Object to dictionary
tasks.statement: Write to_dict(obj): a dictionary built from the instance's attributes (vars). Convert nested objects that have attributes recursively, process lists and tuples element by element (as lists), and leave simple values as they are.
tasks.hint: A helper convert(value): if the value has __dict__, use to_dict; if it is a list/tuple, [convert(x) ...]; otherwise the value itself.

tasks.title: Name of the calling function
tasks.statement: Write caller_name(): it returns the name of the function it was called from (at module level, "<module>"). Use inspect.currentframe() and f_back; don't forget to delete the reference to the frame.
tasks.hint: frame = inspect.currentframe().f_back; name = frame.f_code.co_name; del frame; return name.

tasks.title: Loading an object by a string
tasks.statement: Write load(path): given a string like "package.module.name", it imports the module (importlib.import_module) and returns the object with that name. No such module means ImportError, no such name means AttributeError.
